claim: Pushover sends a message via POST to https://api.pushover.net/1/messages.json, authenticated with an application API token plus the recipient user/group key; messages support title, priority -2 to 2 (emergency), custom sound, supplementary url+url_title, image attachment up to 5MB, and HTML or monospace formatting, delivering to dedicated iOS, Android, and desktop browser push clients.
quote: send a POST request to https://api.pushover.net/1/messages.json with... token (your application's API token), user (your user/group key)... message ... html ... priority ... -2, -1, 0 (default), 1, 2 ... attachment ... url ... a supplementary URL

claim: Pushbullet pushes are created via POST to https://api.pushbullet.com/v2/pushes with an Access-Token header, supporting note, link, and file push types with title/body fields.
quote: POST https://api.pushbullet.com/v2/pushes ... Access-Token: <your_access_token_here> ... type ... note ... title ... body

claim: Pushbullet delivers pushes to Android, iOS, Chrome and Firefox browser extensions, and Windows desktop clients, with free accounts capped at 500 pushes per month.
quote: Pushbullet ... Android ... iOS ... Chrome ... Firefox ... Windows ... limited to 500 pushes per month

claim: Telegram Bot API calls use https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME; sendMessage takes a chat_id, supports parse_mode HTML and MarkdownV2 formatting plus inline-keyboard buttons via reply_markup, and delivers into a Telegram chat conversation (iOS, Android, desktop, web) rather than a dedicated push app.
quote: https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME ... Each bot is given a unique authentication token when it is created ... parse_mode ... MarkdownV2 ... HTML ... Inline keyboard attached to the message

claim: Slack incoming webhooks post a JSON payload (text or Block Kit blocks) to a unique webhook URL that is itself the credential and is bound to a single installer-chosen channel; they cannot upload files, delete posted messages, or override the channel, and deliver into a Slack channel (iOS, Android, desktop, web) rather than a dedicated push app.
quote: Creating an incoming webhook gives you a unique URL to which you send a JSON payload with the message text and some options ... you cannot override the default channel ... Incoming webhooks do not allow you to delete a message after it's been posted

claim: Pushover costs $4.99 USD as a one-time purchase per platform (iPhone/iPad, Android, Desktop) with no subscription, and each user can send up to 10,000 messages/month free.
quote: $4.99 USD one-time purchase on each platform ... Each user can send up to 10,000 messages per month for free.

claim: Starting May 1 2026, Pushover's 10,000 messages/month free quota became per-account (shared across all apps) rather than per-application; Teams get 25,000/month shared.
quote: all applications will share the user's pool of 10,000 free messages per month

claim: Pushbullet Pro is priced at $4.99/month or $39.99/year and includes 100GB of storage plus premium features.
quote: Pushbullet Pro offers premium features and 100GB of storage for $39.99 a year

claim: Pushbullet's free tier is capped at roughly 100 pushes/month, with Pro ($39.99/year or $4.99/month) removing the limit.
quote: 100/month restriction ... $39.99/year or $4.99/month

claim: Telegram's Bot API is completely free with no per-message charges, no monthly API fees, and no limit on the number of bots; costs only arise from self-hosting.
quote: Telegram's Bot API itself is completely free — there are no per-message charges, no monthly API fees, and no limits on the number of bots you can create.

claim: Slack's Free plan provides 90 days of message history and up to 10 app integrations; Pro is roughly €8.25/user/month full price (€6.75 annual).
quote: 90 days of message history ... Up to 10 apps ... €8.25 monthly at full price ... €6.75 per user/month

claim: Slack incoming webhooks work on the Free plan but count toward the 10-app integration cap, and messages older than 90 days become inaccessible (hidden behind a paywall, not deleted).
quote: incoming webhooks are supported on Slack Free and do count toward the 10-app integration cap ... messages older than 90 days become inaccessible

claim: Apprise (16.7k stars) natively supports all four relays via URL schemas: Pushover pover://user@token, Pushbullet pbul://accesstoken, Telegram tgram://bottoken/ChatID, and Slack slack://TokenA/TokenB/TokenC.
quote: pover://user@token ... pbul://accesstoken ... tgram://bottoken/ChatID ... slack://TokenA/TokenB/TokenC/

claim: shoutrrr natively supports Pushover, Pushbullet, Slack and Telegram among its built-in services, with URLs like pushover://shoutrrr:apiToken@userKey, slack://botname@token-a/token-b/token-c, and telegram://token@telegram?chats=@channel.
quote: Discord, Email, Gotify, Google Chat, IFTTT, Join, Mattermost, Matrix, OpsGenie, PushBullet, Pushover, Rocketchat, Slack, Teams, Telegram, and Zulip

claim: shoutrrr is a Go notification library/CLI with roughly 1.6k GitHub stars.
quote: 1.6k stars

claim: Uptime Kuma (87.8k stars) ships built-in notification providers for Telegram, Slack, Pushover and Pushbullet among 90+ total channels.
quote: Notifications via Telegram, Discord, Gotify, Slack, Pushover, Email (SMTP), and 90+ notification services

claim: Home Assistant offers first-class notify integrations for Pushover, Pushbullet, Slack and Telegram (the Telegram bot integration provides actions to send/edit/receive messages).
quote: creates notification actions to send, edit, receive messages or download attachments from a Telegram Bot account

claim: Grafana alerting contact points natively support Slack, Telegram and Pushover integrations, but have no first-class Pushbullet contact point.
quote: Configure Telegram for Alerting ... Configure Slack for Alerting

claim: Watchtower uses shoutrrr as its notification backend, supporting Slack (slack://hook:TOKEN@webhook) and Telegram (telegram://TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHATID) via WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL, but has no native Pushbullet shoutrrr service.
quote: Shoutrrr is the default notification library for Watchtower ... slack://hook:WEBHOOK_TOKEN@webhook ... telegram://TOKEN@telegram?chats=CHATID

claim: n8n ships dedicated built-in nodes for Pushover (Push Message action), Telegram (Send Message/Photo/Document etc.) and Slack, but has no native Pushbullet node.
quote: The Push Message action allows you to send customized push notifications ... Telegram ... Send Message, Send Photo, Send Document

claim: Sending a Telegram message from a container is a curl POST to api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage with chat_id and text parameters.
quote: Sending a notification message to Telegram using its HTTP API via cURL

claim: Each Pushover account may send 10,000 messages per month for free shared across all of the account's applications, with Teams allowing 25,000.
quote: Each Pushover account may send 10,000 messages per month for free, shared across all of the account's applications. Teams organizations can send up to 25,000 messages monthly.

claim: Telegram bots cannot broadcast more than about 30 messages per second; paid broadcasts via BotFather raise this to up to 1000 messages per second.
quote: your bot will not be able to send more than 30 messages per second... Enabling paid broadcasts in @BotFather allows a bot to broadcast up to 1000 messages per second.

claim: Telegram enforces roughly 1 message per second to an individual chat and about 20 messages per minute to a single group/channel, and returns HTTP 429 with retry_after when exceeded.
quote: 1 message per second to individual chats and 20 messages per minute to groups/channels... Telegram returns a 429 error with a retry_after parameter

claim: Telegram's sendMessage text content is limited to 4096 characters.
quote: text for the message content (limited to 4096 characters)

claim: Slack incoming webhooks are rate-limited to roughly 1 message per second per channel with short bursts allowed; exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.
quote: 1 per second with short bursts >1 allowed... Slack responds with an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests error along with a Retry-After HTTP header

claim: Pushbullet limits free (non-Pro) accounts to 500 API-based pushes per month, returning an error once exceeded.
quote: Pushbullet will limit API-based pushes to 500 per month on free accounts starting August 1

claim: A core argument for routing alerts to an external service is that a monitoring system cannot reliably watch itself, so alerting must be independent of the infrastructure it oversees.
quote: Who is monitoring the monitoring system to make sure it's working?

claim: A dead man's switch / watchdog routes an always-firing alert to an external service so that when any part of the local alerting pipeline breaks the external service notices the absence and alerts you.
quote: When anything in your alerting pipeline breaks, the external service will notice that no more alert notifications are coming in and will send you a notification about it.

claim: Self-hosters note that with third-party push relays, mobile push notifications can be significantly delayed, a reliability tradeoff versus latency.
quote: sometimes push notifications to mobile are significantly delayed

claim: Telegram Cloud Chats (private and group chats, which includes all bot traffic) use only server-client encryption and are NOT end-to-end encrypted; only Secret Chats add a client-client E2E layer.
quote: Server-client encryption is used in Cloud Chats (private and group chats), Secret Chats use an additional layer of client-client encryption.
claim_supplement: All messages in secret chats use end-to-end encryption. This means only you and the recipient can read those messages.

claim: A leaked Telegram bot token grants full control of the bot: an attacker can send messages as the bot, read chat history, and access user data, so tokens must be revoked via BotFather if exposed.
quote: An attacker with a bot token can impersonate the bot, send unauthorized messages, and access sensitive chat data.

claim: Real-world incidents show hardcoded Telegram bot tokens leaking, exposing customer support conversations and PII to anyone who finds the token.
quote: Hardcoded Secrets Strike Again: How a Telegram Bot Token Exposed Customer Support and PII

claim: Pushover uses TLS for all transport but stores message content in plain text on its servers (only until delivery); optional client-side E2E since v5.0 can hide content from Pushover's servers.
quote: We use industry-standard TLS (HTTPS) encryption for all communication in Pushover, in every step of the process ... Messages on our servers are stored in plain-text but are only stored long enough to send them out to your devices

claim: Pushover deletes delivered messages from its servers once delivery is verified, deletes undeliverable messages after 21 days, and does not sell/share collected info except for legal requirements or acquisition (using named sub-processors).
quote: Messages delivered to your devices are deleted from Pushover's servers once delivery has been verified. Messages that cannot be verified as delivered are deleted after 21 days.

claim: Pushbullet uploads and stores SMS data, contact lists, and contact images on its servers when SMS/notification sync is enabled, though it states this is never shared with third parties.
quote: If SMS sync is enabled by the user, some SMS data is uploaded and stored on Pushbullet servers in order to facilitate this functionality. None of this information is ever shared with third parties.

claim: Pushbullet has a documented history of Google Play Store privacy-disclosure violations over publishing users' contact and notification data to its servers, reflecting an aggressive notification/SMS-reading posture.
quote: Pushbullet says it has to fight Play Store's automated oversight to stay on Android

claim: Slack workspace owners/admins control retention policies and can configure how long messages and files are kept, meaning message content persists server-side under admin-set policy.
quote: Customize data retention in Slack ... Workspace Owners and Admins can set retention policies for messages and files.

claim: Slack admins can export workspace data; on Enterprise Grid, Discovery API / approved compliance exports can extract private channels and DMs, so deleted messages may already be captured in compliance records.
quote: Workspace Owners can apply to access a self-serve data export tool for messages and file links from public channels, private channels, and DMs in JSON format.

claim: Pushover is run by Pushover, LLC (formerly Superblock, LLC), a private, independently-financed software company in Chicago operating the service since March 2012 — so the Superblock name is a rename, not an acquisition.
quote: Pushover is a service of Pushover, LLC (formerly Superblock, LLC), a private, independently-financed software development company based out of Chicago, Illinois.

claim: Pushover's Android app package name is net.superblock.pushover, reflecting its operating company Superblock/Pushover LLC.
quote: Pushover - net.superblock.pushover

claim: Pushbullet moved previously-free features like universal copy-and-paste and unlimited messaging behind a $4.99/month (or $39.99/year) Pro paywall, capping free message sending (SMS/WhatsApp) at 100/month.
quote: Only Pro users may use universal copy and paste, a feature that has been available in the free version before... Message sending is limited to 100 per month in the free version and unlimited in the Pro version. Pro pricing: $4.99 per month or $39.99 per year.

claim: Pushbullet remains actively maintained in 2026, last updated June 5 2026, and added MMS picture-message support in April 2026 — its SMS feature was not removed, contrary to common 'Pushbullet is dead' chatter.
quote: Pushbullet: SMS on PC and more... enables SMS from your PC and shows your phone's notifications on your desktop.

claim: Pushbullet has suffered eroding community trust as features moved behind Pro and its Chrome extension hit Manifest V3 friction, driving migration toward Microsoft Phone Link and single-purpose tools.
quote: the company introduced a paid Pro tier that moved long-standing features behind a paywall, its Chrome extension ran into Google's Manifest V3 transition, and community trust frayed... widespread migration away from Pushbullet.

claim: Telegram's Bot API is under very active development, shipping Bot API 10.0 on May 8 2026 with roughly 8 versions over 13 months (1-2 month cadence), signalling strong longevity and a large free ecosystem.
quote: Bot API 10.0 (May 8, 2026); Bot API 9.6 (April 3, 2026); Bot API 9.5 (March 1, 2026); Bot API 9.4 (February 9, 2026); Bot API 9.3 (December 31, 2025).

claim: Slack discontinued legacy custom bots on March 31 2025 and will shut off classic apps on November 16 2026, forcing migration of legacy integrations to modern Slack apps.
quote: Beginning March 31, 2025, legacy custom bots will no longer function... Beginning November 16, 2026, classic apps will no longer function. API calls made by a classic apps will be rejected.

claim: Slack labels legacy custom-integration incoming webhooks as outdated, lacking newer features, and 'will be deprecated and possibly removed in the future,' steering users to recreate them inside a Slack app.
quote: Legacy custom integrations are an outdated way for teams to integrate with Slack. They lack newer features and will be deprecated and possibly removed in the future.

claim: Slack's free plan caps usage to 90 days of message/file history and 10 total app/integration slots, materially constraining hobbyist/lab use as a notification target.
quote: you'll be limited to the most recent 90 days of message and file history... You can add up to 10 third-party or custom apps.
